title: Heterogeneous-Goal MAPE-K for Adaptive AI Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a MAPE-K controller that explicitly models heterogeneous requirements—mixing hard thresholds such as safety/cost limits with optimization goals such as task quality and latency—improve adaptation decisions in AI agent workflows compared with single-objective or fixed-policy orchestration?
hypothesis: Extending MAPE-K with explicit heterogeneous requirement handling will reduce unnecessary adaptations and improve overall workflow utility in multi-agent AI systems, especially under uncertainty and changing workload conditions.
motivation: The knowledge base surfaces a concrete open problem: prior self-adaptive systems work explicitly names heterogeneous requirements, including threshold and optimization goals, as future work. At the same time, recently rejected ideas in agentic workflow optimization cluster around routing, uncertainty-aware scheduling, and adaptive orchestration, suggesting that another scheduler variant is unlikely to be novel enough. A stronger gap is to transfer the heterogeneous-requirement formulation from self-adaptive systems into AI agent orchestration, where workflows must jointly satisfy hard constraints such as budget, safety, and context-window limits while optimizing answer quality, latency, and collaboration depth. This creates a clearer research gap than generic uncertainty-aware routing and aligns with the high-priority direction on agentic workflow optimization.
